title: Subtract what is already there
hook: Seven in stock and twelve needed: how many are missing?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Calculate nonnegative replenishment after counting available stock.

misconception: A shopping requirement is always the quantity that must be ordered.
objective: Calculate nonnegative replenishment after counting available stock.

claims.text: Seven usable units are already available. A orders only the gap; B orders the whole requirement. Scaled model; usable stock=7; no hidden commitments.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Required=12, A=5items and B=12items. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["max",0,["-","x",7]]; B="x"; x denotes Required. At x=12, A=5, B=12. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Required quantity minus available stock gives the shortage. The maximum with zero prevents a negative order when stock already covers demand. Existing usable units belong in the calculation.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["max",0,["-","x",7]]; B="x"; x denotes Required. At x=12, A=5, B=12. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: You need nine units and already have twelve usable ones. How many do you order? Correct: 0. The order is the shortage, need minus stock, and never below zero: stock already covers the need.
